title: Heat Capacity and Other Thermodynamic Properties of Aqueous Magnesium Sulfate to 473 K
authors: Ramesh C. Phutela, Kenneth S. Pitzer
experimental_method: Twin-cell Picker-type flow calorimeter (Hastelloy C-276), equal volumetric flow of water and solution at 298.15 K, heater powers adjusted for equal temperature rise; cp of solution from the power ratio with heat-loss correction (eq 1); 348 to 473 K at 20 bar.
uncertainties_stated: phiCp uncertainty from the heat-loss assumption 0.5 to 2.5 J/(K mol) at 348 K, about 4 J/(K mol) at 423 K and 9 J/(K mol) at 473 K; total possible error up to twice these values.
quality_remarks: Calibration and tests with water in both units and with NaCl(aq). Replicate runs at 0.5946 mol/kg, 348.15 K scatter by 10 J/(K mol) (-18.5, -9.7, -20.5). The water heat capacity implied by cp and phiCp is constant within each block to 1e-4 J/(g K) (4.1807, 4.2128, 4.2532, 4.3070, 4.3808, 4.4863 J/(g K)), so cp and phiCp are mutually consistent. Temperature scale not stated. Note for checking: the implied water cp at 348.15 K (4.1807 J/(g K)) is about 0.3 % below the usual value for water near 75 C (about 4.19 J/(g K)); the other blocks are closer to steam-table values. Not investigated; printed numbers kept as is.
